title: A Laravel handler answers 201, 404 and 422 — the status codes callers depend on must be stated, not left to the target framework
sourceContent:
<?php
namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\Customer;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB;

class InvoiceController extends Controller
{
    public function store(Request $request, $customerId)
    {
        // TRAP: three outcomes, three status codes - only one is written out.
        $data = $request->validate(['amount' => 'required|numeric|min:0.01', 'note' => 'nullable|string|max:200']);
        $customer = Customer::find($customerId);
        if ($customer === null) {
            abort(404, 'No such customer');
        }
        $id = DB::table('invoices')->insertGetId([
            'customer_id' => $customer->id, 'amount' => $data['amount'], 'note' => $data['note'] ?? null,
        ]);
        return response()->json(['id' => $id, 'amount' => $data['amount']], 201);
    }
}
notes: Laravel's validate() answers 422 with an errors object on its own, abort(404) answers 404, and the success path answers 201 with the new id. A Spring or ASP.NET Core rewrite returns 200 and its own validation shape unless the spec says otherwise, which breaks every caller that checks the status. The insert is a data access on invoices with bound values.
